description: Verifiable skill credentials on Hedera. Each skill is a soulbound token that levels up or down as the holder's work is reviewed, a reputation oracle scores that work, and companies fund job pools that candidates join with the skills they hold. Your professional reputation travels with you instead of being re-proved at every interview.
role: Lead engineer: built the smart contracts, the API and the web app
contributions: Wrote the four core contracts in Solidity: SkillToken (non-transferable skill credentials with levels), ReputationOracle, TalentPool and Governance, with shared libraries for each
Wrote about 220 contract tests in Hardhat, then deployed all four contracts to Hedera testnet
Built the API in Python and FastAPI: about 75 endpoints for skills, job pools, reputation and governance
Built AI work evaluation with LangChain and Groq: submitted work is assessed and the result feeds the holder's reputation and skill level
Built the web app in Next.js and TypeScript: dashboard, skills, jobs, companies, governance, notifications and settings, with Hedera wallets through WalletConnect
Ported the contracts and front end to Solana as a second version
results: 43 of the project's 49 commits are mine

body.heading: The problem
paragraphs: A developer's reputation is scattered: a CV no one can check, references on one platform, ratings on another. Every new client or employer starts from zero and asks them to prove it again.
TalentChain Pro makes skills a record the developer owns and anyone can verify.

body.heading: How it works
paragraphs: Each skill a developer holds is a soulbound token: it cannot be sold or transferred, and it carries a level, so ReactJS level 3 can become level 4 after good work is reviewed. Work is submitted for evaluation; the AI evaluator assesses it, the reputation oracle records the score, and the skill token moves up or down to match.

Companies create job pools and fund them; developers join with the skill tokens a role asks for, and matches are made from verified skills rather than claims. Governance lets token holders vote on the skill frameworks for each field.

body.heading: Contracts first
paragraphs: The contracts are the source of truth, so I wrote them first and tested them hardest: four contracts with a library each, about 220 tests in Hardhat, then deployment to Hedera testnet. The API and the app read and write through them rather than keeping a separate copy of who holds what.

body.heading: Built with
paragraphs: Solidity and Hardhat on Hedera for the contracts; Python, FastAPI, LangChain and Groq for the API and the AI evaluator; Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind and WalletConnect for the app. A Solana version of the contracts and front end followed.
